question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=3t-2{t}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=3t-2{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(0)=0,\,p(1)=1,\,p(2)=-2.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(0)p(0)+p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(0)]^{2}+[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
